title: Space-bounded clean simulation of a machine bank
statement: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $(M_j)_{j<d}$ be finite-state Boolean Turing machines. For each $j<d$, let $A_j$ be a language of Boolean words and $s_j$ a space bound, and suppose $M_j$ decides $A_j$ using at most $s_j(n)$ visited work-tape cells on inputs of length $n$. Then, for every $j<d$ and Boolean input $V$, the bank machine started in the state corresponding to $M_j$'s initial state halts with output consisting of the single bit indicating whether $V\in A_j$, has all work tapes blank and all work-tape heads at the origin, and throughout the run every head position has absolute value at most $\max(s_j(|V|),1)$.
hypotheses_covered: Natural number $d$ and family of finite-state Boolean machines $(M_j)_{j<d}$
